chapter: Casa, Zeb Lenard and Little Joe
title: Kid Shots, cornetist who deputised for Little Joe
summary: Vincent calls Kid Shots a good cornet player who liked whiskey and filled in for Little Joe for two weeks. He says dance-hall rules about children hurt their work.

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: He don't play no more. I don't play, dude. Kid shots.

How about kid shots? Oh, you remember kid shots? Oh, good. Yeah. Yeah. He was another good corner player. Uh... I look ahead of him up, too. Ooh, that man can drink some whiskey. Yeah, I mean... Well, kid shots was good.

Say, was he reliable? Yeah. Good, I... He played in the little Joe's place once. Joe had his teeth fixed, you know. Played about two weeks. People like to throw the place down in South Carolina, you know. They pay for white people, you know. Down on, uh... Clayborne and Frenchman. And then they stopped, they stopped them once. On the count of the, uh... You know, the people bring their children there. And that just made everything run down, you know. And then it opened up again that they could bring their children there, you know. They had the children in the cash and everything. They had the children in the cash and everything. They just made us lose out, you know. Especially if we pack and jams four times a week. We had to just cut that out with, you know, nobody, you see. How about Albert Nicholas? How about Albert Nicholas? How about Albert Nicholas?
